verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; no STOP (no UB, ABI regression or hidden obligation); three findings repaired (one failure-path allocation divergence, one secret-residue plus release-coordinate class, one allocator-seam release-coordinate class).
scope: Per-file contract audit of provider ML-KEM key management, the MLX hybrid KEM, RSA asymmetric cipher and RSASVE KEM, the default-provider security checks and digest map, provider seeding up-calls and the generic/AES symmetric-key management units. All eight entries were the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt; none was deferred.

defects.description: mlx_kem_decapsulate assigned the ECDH context and then unconditionally called EVP_PKEY_new() before testing the context, so a failed EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_pkey still allocated the peer key. The authority guards the context first and only then allocates the peer, so under allocator-failure injection the Rust unit produced one extra EVP_PKEY allocation. The context-null arm now breaks the end block before the peer allocation; success-path behaviour is unchanged.

defects.class: secret residue plus allocator-seam release coordinate
defects.description: Both OAEP scratch buffers (tbuf) were plain OwnedBuf::new blocks that recorded the allocation line as their release line. The encrypt scratch holds the OAEP-padded plaintext and the decrypt scratch holds the RSA decrypted EM, yet the authority's plain OPENSSL_free was mirrored with no cleansing. Each handle now uses new_cleansed_released at the authority's own allocation and release coordinates (rsa_enc.c.in 197/202/215/220 for encrypt; 272/281/289/304/311 for decrypt) and set_release_line selects the correct early-arm coordinate. Cleanse-before-free is a deliberate improvement over the authority's OPENSSL_free and is not observable through the API.

Eight scratch handles recorded their allocation coordinate as their release coordinate: the pairwise ctext block (alloc 115, tail free 158), the export public/seed/private/encoded-DK blocks (269/339, 283/337, 289/338, 294/338), check_prvenc (377/383), and the replacement propq strdup (old free 734, new alloc 735). In addition, ml_kem_load's success and err arms shared LINE_LOAD_CLEAR=535, a line that is not a free site at all (the authority frees at 558 on success and 565 on error). new_*_released constructors and set_release_line now carry the separate pairs; allocation sizes and every successful-path release remain unchanged.

documentation_corrections: ml_kem_kmgmt's load_err doc now names the detach lines 531-535 and the err-arm free at 565, and the success arm names LINE_LOAD_CLEAR=558.
rsa_enc's OAEP scratch comments now name the allocation and each early release coordinate at the .c.in lines the campaign treats as the pinned authority for this generated unit.
retained_obligations: Dispatch callbacks receive borrowed raw pointers under the provider ABI; the key/context lifetime is the EVP caller's obligation (unchanged).

provider_seeding's eight file statics are written by ossl_prov_seeding_from_dispatch during provider initialisation and read by the up-calls; provider init is serialised by the provider core, as in the authority.
ProvMlxKemCtx.key is borrowed, not owned; the MLX key outlives the operation context under the KEM dispatch contract.
ProvRsaCtx/ProvMlxKemCtx/ProvSkey destructors rely on the OB-3 zero-validity and member-body contracts; all three are covered by the zero_state_sweep controls.
